title: Natural law: morality you can reason about
tagline: Why right and wrong are not just opinion, and how to speak about it kindly to people who do not share your faith.
whyItMatters: Many people feel that moral claims are either private tastes or religious rules. Natural law says some things about good and harm can be known by reason, and this is how the Church speaks to everyone.

mindset.tip: Ask what the person is worried about before you explain anything. Most objections come from a fear of being judged or controlled (1 Peter 3:15-16).
Start from experience everyone shares: we feel wronged when we are treated unfairly. Kreeft uses exactly this move.
Use reasons the other person can test, not only quotations from Scripture. The Church itself teaches that conscience and reason can find moral truth (CCC 1954-1960; Romans 2:14-15).
Keep a clear difference between what the law should forbid and what a person should choose; the second is wider. Admit that hard cases are hard.
Remember that conscience must be formed, not just followed (CCC 1783-1785). Be willing to ask what you have not yet understood.
